summary: One P&R iteration (it1) was run with FP_CORE_UTIL 45, PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT 55.0, MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT 10; it reported no problems and no parameters were changed. The tool data for it1 shows route_drc_errors 0, antenna_violating_nets 0, antenna_violating_pins 0, disconnected_pins 0, max slew/cap/fanout violations 0, worst setup slack 2.0134099402044963 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60) and worst hold slack 0.11395409938206096 ns (min_ff_n40C_1v95) over 9 corners, wirelength 1563 um, utilization 0.507475, worst CTS tree skew 0.003713 ns against a 1.0 ns target. No routing congestion/overflow figure is present in the input data. These are flow-reported values; the S2S runtime decides pass/fail.
assumptions: No clock gating cells are used: the spec lists low-power modes and clock gating as out of scope, and the tool data reports none.
Tess and Sentinel show 0.0 spend, read as no billed model usage in this run.
The 1.0 ns CTS skew target (cts_target_ns / target_ns) comes from the tool data, not from the spec.
The pnr_report.json iteration it1 is the final P&R state. Its slack values are post-route worst slacks from the flow's STA.
The single entry in reports/pnr_iterations.json (iteration 1, tag it1) is the final P&R state; no other iterations exist.
The skew target is the target_ns value of 1.0 in reports/cts_tool.json; the spec does not state a skew target, so its origin is assumed to be the flow configuration.
antenna_violating_nets/pins are from the flow's antenna check after routing.
clock_buffers = 3 counts buffers inserted in the clock tree; timing_repair_buffers = 22 are data-path buffers and not part of the clock tree.
division_cost.json contains run spend by agent only. It has no budget or weekly forecast, so neither is stated as a number.
hold_ws_after_cts_by_corner and setup_ws_after_cts_by_corner are worst slacks in ns as reported by the flow's STA after CTS.

reported_skew_ns includes the 0.25 ns clock_uncertainty_ns; tree_skew_ns is the skew of the clock tree itself, and that is the value compared with the target (the data shows reported_skew_ns = clock_uncertainty_ns + tree_skew_ns in the setup views).
route_drc_errors is the detailed-router DRC count, not a Magic/KLayout signoff DRC on the final GDS.
route_drc_errors is the router's count and is not a signoff Magic/KLayout DRC on the final GDS.
setup_ws_by_corner and hold_ws_by_corner in pnr_iterations.json are post-route worst slacks in ns as reported by the flow's STA; positive means the path meets the constraint.
source_latency_ns is read as the clock insertion latency from the clock port to the register clock pins; target_latency_ns (negative values) is quoted as given and not interpreted further.
utilization 0.507475 in pnr_iterations.json is post-placement/route cell utilization (including inserted buffers), which is why it is higher than the floorplan utilization 0.484219.

The min_* and max_* corners (6 of the 9 corners with skew data) have no post-CTS slack in this data; hold at min_ff_n40C_1v95 and max_ff_n40C_1v95 is the most likely to be tight and should be reported by Chronos (STA) before REQ-011 is judged.

messages.summary: Clock clk (100 MHz, 10 ns per spec): the tool data reports a worst clock-tree skew of 0.003713 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60 setup view) against a target_ns of 1.0, across 9 corners, with 3 clock buffers. Source latency ranges from 0.156097 ns (min_ff_n40C_1v95, setup) to 0.405277 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60, setup). Post-CTS hold worst slack is positive in the 3 corners reported (smallest 0.07729696268507003 ns at nom_ff_n40C_1v95); 0 hold buffers and 22 timing-repair buffers are reported. Hold slack after CTS is only given for the 3 nom corners, so the min/max corners are not covered by this data. No check is claimed passed here; the runtime runs the real checks.

Wrote the Division 3 (Zone 3) VP report for counter8 at place_route. Synthesis, floorplan, CTS and P&R iteration it1 were delivered. The flow reports 0 route DRC, antenna, slew, cap and fanout problems, and positive setup and hold slack in all 9 corners (worst setup 2.0134099402044963 ns at max_ss_100C_1v60, worst hold 0.11395409938206096 ns at min_ff_n40C_1v95). Risks are the missing signoff DRC/LVS (REQ-013), the missing congestion data, the thin hold margin, an unexplained jump in setup slack between CTS and route, open spec questions on corners and PDK release, and DFT that cannot be done in Phase 0. Cost is reported per agent only, because no budget figure was supplied. The report lists 4 decisions for the human, each with a recommendation.

self_assessment.reason: All numbers are copied directly from the three input reports; the data set is small (one iteration). Confidence is limited only by what the inputs do not contain (congestion/overflow, signoff DRC/LVS), which is listed as open.
